paragraphs: FedEx Corporation ("FedEx") was incorporated in Delaware on October 2, 1997 to serve as the parent holding company and provide strategic direction to the FedEx portfolio of companies. FedEx provides customers and businesses worldwide with a broad portfolio of transportation, e-commerce, and business services, offering integrated business solutions utilizing its flexible, efficient, and intelligent global network.

Our website is located at fedex.com. Detailed information about our services, solutions, and corporate responsibility initiatives can be found on our website. In addition, we make our Annual Reports on Form 10-K, Quarterly Reports on Form 10-Q, Current Reports on Form 8-K, and all exhibits and amendments to such reports available, free of charge, through our website, as soon as reasonably practicable on the day they are filed with or furnished to the SEC. The Investor Relations page of our website, investors.fedex.com, contains a significant amount of information about FedEx, including our SEC filings and financial and other information for investors. The information that we post on the Investor Relations page of our website could be deemed to be material information. We encourage investors, the media, and others interested in FedEx to visit this website from time to time, as information is updated and new information is posted. The information on our website, however, is not incorporated by reference in, and does not form part of, this Annual Report.

Effective June 1, 2026, we changed our fiscal year end from May 31 to December 31. As a result, we will report operating results covering the seven-month transition period from June 1, 2026, through December 31, 2026 (the "Transition Period"), in a Transition Report on Form 10-K. Following the Transition Period, we will report our operating results on a calendar-year basis, beginning with the fiscal year ending December 31, 2027. Except as otherwise specified, any reference to a year in this Annual Report indicates our fiscal year ended May 31, 2026 or ended May 31 of the year referenced, and comparisons are to the corresponding period of the prior year.

In December 2024, we announced that FedEx's Board of Directors decided to pursue a full separation of FedEx's less-than-truckload freight transportation services business conducted through FedEx Freight, Inc. ("FedEx Freight"). The FedEx Freight business also included FedEx Custom Critical, Inc. ("FedEx Custom Critical"), LTL Select, and other operations historically included within our FedEx Freight reporting segment. On May 13, 2026, the FedEx Board of Directors declared a pro rata dividend of 80.1% of the outstanding shares of common stock of FedEx Freight Holding Company, Inc. ("FedEx Freight Holding") to FedEx's stockholders of record as of the close of business on May 15, 2026 (the "Record Date") to achieve the separation (the "Spin-Off"). On June 1, 2026, FedEx stockholders received one share of FedEx Freight common stock for every two shares of FedEx common stock held as of the Record Date. FedEx retained 19.9% of the outstanding shares of FedEx Freight common stock. As a result of the Spin-Off, effective June 1, 2026, FedEx will no longer consolidate the FedEx Freight business and FedEx Freight is no longer a reportable segment.

Prior to the Spin-Off, our reportable segments were Federal Express Corporation ("Federal Express"), the world's largest express transportation company and a leading North American provider of small-package ground delivery services, and FedEx Freight. For financial information concerning our reportable segments in place prior to the Spin-Off, refer to "Item 7. Management's Discussion and Analysis of Results of Operations and Financial Condition" and "Item 8. Financial Statements and Supplementary Data" of this Annual Report. Part I of this Annual Report contains certain references to the financial and operational performance of our reportable segments in place prior to the Spin-Off. Additional information regarding our reportable segments in place during 2026 and 2025 can be found in "Item 1. Business" and "Item 2. Properties" of our Annual Report for the year ended May 31, 2025.

Following the Spin-Off and beginning the first quarter of the Transition Period, we realigned our internal reporting and management structure, resulting in the identification of two new reportable segments: Express U.S. Domestic and Express International. Prior to this change, these two segments comprised the Federal Express reportable segment. In addition, FedEx Logistics, Inc. ("FedEx Logistics"), which provides customs brokerage and global ocean and air freight forwarding, was moved from "Corporate, other, and eliminations" to Express International. These changes reflect the realignment of our organizational structure and reporting regularly provided to our chief operating decision maker to assess performance and allocate resources. These changes had no impact on our consolidated results of operations or financial position. For more information about our new reportable segments effective June 1, 2026, please refer to the "Business Segments" below.

The collective FedEx brand gives us our competitive edge. Further, our strategy allows us to manage our business as a portfolio, in the long-term best interest of the enterprise. As a result, we base decisions on capital investment and service additions or enhancements

upon achieving the highest overall long-term return on invested capital for our business as a whole. We focus on making appropriate investments in the technology and assets necessary to optimize our long-term earnings performance and cash flow. Our business strategy also provides flexibility in structuring our network to align with varying macroeconomic conditions and customer demand for the market segments in which the customer operates, allowing us to leverage and manage change. Volatility, uncertainty, and innovation have become the norms in the global transportation market, and we are able to use our flexibility to accommodate changing conditions in the global economy.

For more than 50 years, we have been building networks that have created a differentiated and unmatched portfolio of services while continuously evolving to meet the changing needs of our customers and the market by connecting people and possibilities. We are shifting from a collection of separate but powerful operations to one integrated, flexible, efficient, and intelligent network that delivers better service, runs on a modern technology stack and has a structurally lower cost to serve. We continue to evolve to improve our operational efficiency, enhance profitability, and build a simplified experience to better serve our customers.

In connection with our one FedEx consolidation plan, on June 1, 2024, FedEx Ground Package System, Inc. ("FedEx Ground") and FedEx Corporate Services, Inc. were merged into Federal Express Corporation ("Federal Express"), becoming a single company operating a unified, fully integrated air-ground express network under the respected FedEx brand.

In 2026, we continued our network transformation. Through Network 2.0, we continue to transform our surface network in the U.S. and Canada by modernizing and consolidating our sortation facilities and equipment, reducing pickup-and-delivery routes, and optimizing our enterprise linehaul network by moving beyond discrete collaboration to an end-to-end optimized network. Network 2.0 has been fully implemented in Canada and we expect to complete the U.S. implementation by the end of calendar year 2027. With Tricolor, we are redesigning our international air network by deploying our aircraft strategically to optimize asset utilization and enable a focus on growth in the premium global freight market. Internationally, we are focused on leveraging tools and best practices from our U.S. operations to transform our international operations by scaling to higher-value international mix, reengineering the network, and driving end-to-end process efficiencies. See "Business Segments" below, "Item 1A. Risk Factors," and "Item 7. Management's Discussion and Analysis of Results of Operations and Financial Condition" of this Annual Report for more information on our transformation programs.

Our digital transformation is underpinned by our digital backbone and artificial intelligence ("AI") capabilities, enabling intelligent orchestration, standardization, and digitized and AI-enabled workflows that drive faster response, fewer exceptions, and lower our cost to serve. Our digital transformation is focused on efficiency, differentiation, and new value creation. The size and scale of our global network gives us key insights into global supply chains and trends. This foundation provides an immense amount of data we can use to build better insights, improve the customer experience, and differentiate our service offerings.

"Safety Above All" is the first and foremost value in every aspect of our business. We are committed to making our workplaces and communities safer for our team members, customers, and the public. This philosophy is embedded in our day-to-day work through rigorous policies, continual education and engagement, and investments in technology designed to prevent accidents.

Through our global transportation, information technology, and retail networks, we help to facilitate an ongoing and unprecedented expansion of customer access — to goods, services, and information. We believe it would be extremely difficult, costly, and time-consuming to replicate our global network, which reflects decades of investment, innovation, and expertise, includes the world's largest all-cargo air fleet, and connects more than 99% of the world's gross domestic product. We continue to position our company and team members to facilitate and capitalize on this access and to achieve stronger long-term growth, productivity, and profitability.

In addition to the other information set forth in this Annual Report, you should carefully consider the following factors, which could materially affect our business, reputation, operating results (including components of our financial results), financial condition, cash flows, liquidity, and the price of our common stock. Although the risks below are organized by headings and each risk is discussed separately, many are interrelated.

We are directly affected by the state of the global economy and geopolitical developments. While macroeconomic risks apply to most companies, we are particularly vulnerable. The transportation industry is highly cyclical and especially susceptible to trends in economic activity. Our primary business is to transport goods, so our business levels are directly tied to the purchase and production of goods and the rate of global trade growth — key macroeconomic measurements influenced by, among other things: inflation and deflation; international trade policies and relations; supply chain disruptions; interest rates; currency exchange rates; labor costs and unemployment levels; fuel and energy prices; inventory levels; spending patterns (including shifts from goods to services and vice versa); disposable income; debt levels; credit availability; political uncertainty; public health crises; geopolitical tensions or conflicts; emerging global trade corridors; and changes to social conditions and regulations. When individuals and companies purchase and produce fewer goods, we transport fewer shipments, and as companies move manufacturing closer to consumer markets and expand the number of distribution centers, we transport shipments shorter distances, which materially and adversely affects our revenue per shipment and results of operations. Certain manufacturers and retailers are also making investments to produce and store goods in closer proximity to supply chains and consumers. Further, the scale of our operations and our relatively high fixed-cost structure, particularly with respect to our air network, make it difficult to quickly adjust to match shifting volume levels.

The decline in U.S. imports of consumer goods that started in late 2022, along with slowed global industrial production, has contributed to continued weakened business conditions for the transportation industry leading to lower shipment volumes. Additionally, recent changes in U.S. and international trade policy have further weakened business conditions for the transportation industry. Inflation and elevated interest rates are negatively affecting consumer and business spending, and we expect inflation and elevated interest rates to continue to negatively affect our results for the remainder of calendar year 2026. See "Item 7. Management's Discussion and Analysis of Results of Operations and Financial Condition" of this Annual Report for more information.

Moreover, given the nature of our business and our global operations, political, economic, and other conditions in foreign countries and regions, including international taxes, government-to-government relations, the typically more volatile economies of emerging markets, and geopolitical risks such as the ongoing conflicts between Russia and Ukraine, the United States and Iran, and other

hostilities in the Middle East, may materially and adversely affect our business and results of operations. For example, our services in Ukraine remain limited, our services in Belarus remain suspended, we have exited our operations in Russia, and our services in the Middle East are impacted. The broader consequences, duration, and evolving nature of these conflicts, which have included and may include further sanctions, embargoes, regional instability, and geopolitical shifts; airspace bans relating to certain routes, or strategic decisions to alter certain routes; potential retaliatory action by foreign governments and other groups against us; and the increased tensions between the United States and countries in which we operate, cannot be predicted.

To the extent the continued conflicts between Russia and Ukraine, and the United States and Iran, and hostilities in the Middle East, or subsequent similar conflicts or hostilities, materially and adversely affect our business, they may also have the effect of heightening many other risks disclosed in this Annual Report, any of which could materially and adversely affect our business and results of operations. Such risks include, but are not limited to, disruptions to our global technology infrastructure, including through cyberattack or cyber-intrusion, ransomware attack, or malware attack; adverse changes in international trade policies; increased costs and unavailability of fuel; our ability to implement and execute our business strategy, particularly with regard to our international business; disruptions in global supply chains, which can limit the access of Federal Express and our service providers to vehicles and other key capital resources and increase our costs and could affect our ability to achieve our goal of carbon neutrality for our global operations by calendar 2040; our ability to maintain our strong reputation and the value of the FedEx brand; terrorist activities targeting transportation infrastructure; our exposure to foreign currency fluctuations; and constraints, volatility, or disruption in the capital markets.

This Management's Discussion and Analysis of Results of Operations and Financial Condition ("MD&A") of FedEx Corporation ("FedEx") is composed of three major sections: Results of Operations and Outlook, Financial Condition, and Critical Accounting Estimates. These sections include the following information:

•Results of operations includes an overview of our consolidated 2026 results compared to 2025 results. This section also includes a discussion of key actions and events that impacted our results. The results discussed for the year ended May 31, 2026 include the operations of FedEx Freight for the full fiscal year. Discussion and analysis of 2024 results and year-over-year comparisons between 2025 results and 2024 results can be found in "Item 7. Management's Discussion and Analysis of Results of Operations and Financial Condition" of our Annual Report on Form 10-K ("Annual Report") for the year ended May 31, 2025.

•The overview is followed by a discussion of historical operating results for our business segments during 2026 and 2025, as well as a financial summary and analysis for each of our transportation segments in place during 2026 and 2025. In light of our change in fiscal year end from May 31 to December 31, the discussion includes our outlook for the twelve months ending December 31 ("calendar year"). Except as otherwise specified, any reference to a year indicates our fiscal year ending May 31, 2026 or ended May 31 of the year referenced, and comparisons are to the corresponding period of the prior year.
•Our financial condition is reviewed through an analysis of key elements of our liquidity and capital resources, financial commitments, and liquidity outlook for calendar year 2026.

•Critical accounting estimates discusses those financial statement elements that we believe are most important to understanding the material judgments and assumptions incorporated in our financial results.

The discussion in MD&A should be read in conjunction with the other sections of this Annual Report, particularly "Item 1. Business," "Item 1A. Risk Factors," and "Item 8. Financial Statements and Supplementary Data."

We provide a broad portfolio of transportation, e-commerce, and business services, offering integrated business solutions utilizing our flexible, efficient, and intelligent global network. During 2026 and 2025, our primary operating companies were Federal Express Corporation ("Federal Express"), the world's largest express transportation company and a leading North American provider of small-package ground delivery services, and FedEx Freight, Inc. ("FedEx Freight"), a leading North American provider of less-than-truckload ("LTL") freight transportation services. For those periods, Federal Express and FedEx Freight represented our major service lines and constituted our reportable segments.

This MD&A is based on our segment reporting that was in effect during 2026 and 2025. On June 1, 2026, we completed the Spin-Off. Effective as of this date, we will no longer consolidate FedEx Freight and FedEx Freight is no longer a reportable segment. headings: 本公司、其他及消除項目
paragraphs: FedEx Corporation ("FedEx") 於 1997 年 10 月 2 日在特拉華州成立，作為母公司及提供戰略方向給 FedEx 各家公司。FedEx 為全球的客戶與企業提供廣泛的運輸、電子商務及企業服務，透過其靈活、高效且智能的全球網路，提供整合的企業解決方案。

我們的網站位於 fedex.com。有關我們的服務、解決方案及企業責任計畫的詳細資訊，可於網站上找到。此外，我們會將年度報告（Form 10-K）、季報（Form 10-Q）、現況報告（Form 8-K）以及所有附屬文件及修正案，免費提供於網站上，於合理可行的時間內，於向美國證券交易委員會（SEC）提交或提供後立即公開。我們網站的投資人關係頁（investors.fedex.com）包含大量關於 FedEx 的資訊，包括 SEC 檔案及投資人用的財務及其他資訊。我們於投資人關係頁上發布的資訊可能被視為重要資訊。我們鼓勵投資人、媒體及其他對 FedEx 感興趣的人士，定期造訪此網站，因資訊會持續更新並新增資訊。然而，我們網站上的資訊並未被引用於此年度報告，亦不構成此年度報告的一部分。

自 2026 年 6 月 1 日起，我們將財務年度結算日從 5 月 31 日改為 12 月 31 日。因此，我們將在 2026 年 6 月 1 日至 2026 年 12 月 31 日（稱為「過渡期」）這七個月的過渡期間，發布一份 Form 10-K 的過渡報告。過渡期後，我們將以財務年度為基礎報告營運成果，從 2027 年 12 月 31 日結算的財務年度開始。除非另有說明，本年度報告中提及的任何一年均指我們 2026 年 5 月 31 日結算的財務年度，或指所提及年份的 5 月 31 日結算的財務年度，且比較資料為前一年的對應期間。

2024 年 12 月，我們宣佈 FedEx 督導委員會決定追求將 FedEx Freight, Inc.（"FedEx Freight"）所經營的零擔貨運服務業務完全分離。FedEx Freight 也包含 FedEx Custom Critical, Inc.（"FedEx Custom Critical"）、LTL Select 及其他歷史屬於 FedEx Freight 報告分部的業務。2026 年 5 月 13 日，FedEx 督導委員會宣佈，向於 2026 年 5 月 15 日收市時為 FedEx 股東的股東，發放 FedEx Freight Holding Company, Inc.（"FedEx Freight Holding"）已發行普通股的 80.1% 純粹股息（"Spin-Off"）。2026 年 6 月 1 日，FedEx 股東根據 2026 年 5 月 15 日收市時所持有的 FedEx 普通股數量，每持有兩股 FedEx 普通股，可獲得一股 FedEx Freight 普通股。FedEx 保留 FedEx Freight 普通股已發行股份的 19.9%。由於 Spin-Off 的實施，自 2026 年 6 月 1 日起，FedEx 將不再將 FedEx Freight 會計入合併財務報表，且 FedEx Freight 不再為應報告分部。

在 Spin-Off 之前，我們的應報告分部為 Federal Express Corporation（"Federal Express"），為全球最大之快遞運輸公司，並為北美地區小包裹地面配送服務的主要提供者，以及 FedEx Freight。有關 Spin-Off 之前應報告分部的財務資訊，請參閱本年度報告的「項目 7. 管理層對營運結果與財務狀況之討論與分析」及「項目 8. 財務報表與補充資料」。本年度報告的第一部分包含某些關於 Spin-Off 之前應報告分部的財務與營運表現的參考資訊。有關 2026 年及 2025 年期間應報告分部的更多資訊，請參閱我們 2025 年 5 月 31 日結算年度報告的「項目 1. 企業業務」及「項目 2. 不動產」。

在 Spin-Off 後，並於過渡期的第一季開始，我們重新調整內部報表與管理架構，導致識別出兩個新的應報告分部：Express U.S. Domestic 與 Express International。在調整前，這兩個分部屬於 Federal Express 的應報告分部。此外，FedEx Logistics, Inc.（"FedEx Logistics"），提供報關經紀及全球海洋與空運貨運服務，已從 "企業、其他及消除項目" 移至 Express International。這些調整反映我們組織架構與報表的重新調整，以提供給首席營運決策者定期的資訊，用以評估營運表現與資源配置。這些調整對我們的合併營運成果與財務狀況無影響。如需關於 2026 年 6 月 1 日生效的新應報告分部的更多資訊，請參閱下方的「業務分部」。
FedEx 品牌集合使我們擁有競爭優勢。此外，我們的策略允許我們將業務視為一個組合，以企業長期的最佳利益來管理。因此，我們的決策基於對整體業務的最高長期投資回報率。我們專注於適當投資於必要的技術與資產，以優化長期獲利表現與現金流。我們的業務策略也提供靈活性，以調整網路結構，配合不同的總體經濟條件與客戶所處市場段落的客戶需求，使我們能運用靈活性來應對全球經濟的變化。
不確定性、創新與波動已成為全球運輸市場的常態，我們能運用靈活性來適應全球經濟的變化條件。
在超過 50 年的時間裡，我們一直在建設網路，這些網路創造了差異化且無可比擬的服務組合，同時持續進化以符合客戶與市場的變動需求，透過連接人們與可能性。我們正在從一組獨立但強大的運營轉變為一個整合、靈活、高效且智能的網路，提供更優質的服務，運行在現代化的技術架構上，並具有結構性較低的服務成本。我們持續進化以提高運營效率、增強利潤率，並建立簡化體驗以更好地服務客戶。

根據我們的 FedEx 整合計畫，於 2024 年 6 月 1 日，FedEx Ground Package System, Inc. ("FedEx Ground") 與 FedEx Corporate Services, Inc. 合併至 Federal Express Corporation ("Federal Express")，成為一家單一公司，運營一個統一且完全整合的空地快遞網路，並以受尊重的 FedEx 品牌進行營運。

在 2026 年，我們持續進行網路轉型。透過 Network 2.0，我們持續轉型美國與加拿大的地面網路，透過現代化與整合我們的分揀設施與設備，減少取件與配送路線，並透過從分散合作轉向端到端優化網路，來優化我們的企業長途運輸網路。Network 2.0 已經在加拿大完全實施，我們預期會在 2027 年財務年度結束前完成美國的實施。透過 Tricolor，我們正在重新設計國際航空網路，透過戰略性部署飛機以優化資產使用率，並聚焦於高價值全球貨運市場的成長。國際上，我們專注於運用我們美國運營的工具與最佳實務，來轉型國際運營，透過擴展至更高價值的國際組合、重新設計網路，並推動端到端流程效率。請參閱本年度報告的 "業務分部" 部分、"第 1A 項 風險因素"，以及 "第 7 項 管理層對營運與財務狀況的討論與分析" 以取得更多有關我們轉型計畫的資訊。
我們的數位轉型是以我們的數位基礎設施與人工智慧 ("AI") 能力為基礎，使我們能實現智能協調、標準化，以及數位化與 AI 使能的作業流程，以實現更快的回應、較少的異常，並降低我們的服務成本。我們的數位轉型聚焦於效率、差異化與新價值創造。我們全球網路的規模與規模，使我們能掌握全球供應鏈與趨勢的重要見解。這個基礎提供了大量數據，我們可以用來建立更好的見解、改善客戶體驗，並差異化我們的服務方案。
"安全為首要價值" 是我們業務各方面最重要的價值。我們致力於讓我們的員工、客戶與公眾的作業環境與社區更安全。這種哲學透過嚴謹的政策、持續的教育與參與，以及投資於預防事故的科技，融入我們的日常作業中。
透過我們的全球運輸、資訊科技與零售網路，我們協助促進客戶對商品、服務與資訊的持續且前所未有的擴張性接觸。我們認為要複製我們的全球網路將極其困難、昂貴且耗時，這反映了數十年的投資、創新與專業知識，包含世界上規模最大的全貨運航空艦隊，並連接超過 99% 的全球總體經濟產出。我們持續定位我們的公司與員工，以促進並把握這項接觸，並實現更強的長期成長、生產力與利潤率。

退休計畫 MTM 調整
paragraphs: 本公司管理層對營運成果與財務狀況之分析（"MD&A"）由三個主要部分組成：營運成果與展望、財務狀況，以及關鍵會計估計。這些部分包含以下資訊：
•營運成果包含對我們合併財務報表中2026年度結果與2025年度結果之概覽。此部分亦包含對影響我們結果之關鍵行動與事件之討論。2026年度結算日為2026年5月31日之結果包含FedEx Freight全年營運。2024年度結果之討論與年度對比分析，可於我們2025年度結算日為2025年5月31日之年報（"年報"）中"第7項 管理層對營運成果與財務狀況之分析"找到。
•概覽後，將討論我們業務分部在2026與2025年度之歷史營運結果，以及各運輸分部在2026與2025年度之財務總結與分析。因我們財務年度結算日由2026年5月31日變更為2026年12月31日，討論中包含我們對2026年12月31日結算日（"會計年度"）之展望。除非另有說明，任何提及年份皆指我們2026年5月31日結算之財務年度，或為該年份結算日之財務年度，且比較為前一年相同期間。
•我們財務狀況透過對我們流動性與資本資源、財務承諾及會計年度2026之流動性展望之分析來評估。
•關鍵會計估計討論那些我們認為最重要以理解我們財務結果中所包含之重大判斷與假設之財務報表項目。
MD&A之討論應與本年報之其他部分一併閱讀，特別是"第1項 事業"、"第1A項 風險因素"，以及"第8項 財務報表與補充資料"。

我們提供廣泛之運輸、電商與企業服務，透過我們靈活、高效且智能之全球網路，提供整合式企業解決方案。在2026與2025年度，我們主要營運公司為Federal Express Corporation（"Federal Express"），為全球最大之快遞運輸公司，並為北美地區小包件地面配送服務之領導者，以及FedEx Freight, Inc.（"FedEx Freight"），為北美地區貨運服務之領導者，提供小於卡車載重（"LTL"）貨運服務。在這些期間，Federal Express與FedEx Freight為我們主要服務線，並構成我們應報告分部。
本MD&A基於2026與2025年度有效之分部報告。於2026年6月1日，我們完成分拆。自該日期起，我們將不再合併FedEx Freight，且FedEx Freight不再為應報告分部。對我們運輸分部之參考，包含Federal Express分部與FedEx Freight分部。請參閱下方"應報告分部"與"第1項 事業"以取得更多資訊。
瞭解我們營運成果所必需的關鍵指標包括：
•根據總體經濟因素及全球經濟情況，客戶對我們各項服務的總體需求；
•透過我們網路所提供的運輸服務數量，主要以我們的平均每日運量及貨物重量與尺寸來衡量；
•客戶購買服務的組合；
•我們為服務所獲得的價格，主要以每件貨物或每磅的收入（或每批貨物或每百磅的收入，針對零擔貨運服務）來衡量；
•我們管理成本結構（資本支出及營運費用）以配合運量變動的能力；
除本年度報告中所載之其他資訊外，您應謹慎考量下列因素，這些因素可能重大影響本公司業務、聲譽、營運結果（包括財務結果之組成部分）、財務狀況、現金流、流動性及本公司普通股之價格。雖然下列風險係以標題分類，且每項風險均單獨討論，但許多風險彼此相關。

本公司直接受到全球經濟狀況及地緣政治發展之影響。雖然宏觀經濟風險適用於大多數公司，但本公司尤其容易受到影響。運輸業具有高度週期性，且特別容易受到經濟活動趨勢之影響。本公司主要業務為運輸貨物，因此本公司業務水準與貨物之購買與生產以及全球貿易成長率直接相關——這些為總體經濟指標，受諸如通貨膨脹與通貨緊縮、國際貿易政策與關係、供應鏈中斷、利率、貨幣兌換率、勞動成本與失業率、燃料與能源價格、存貨水準、支出模式（包括從貨物轉向服務或反之亦然）、可支配所得、負債水準、信貸可得性、政治不確定性、公共衛生危機、地緣政治緊張或衝突、新興全球貿易走廊以及社會條件與規範之變動等因素影響。當個人與公司購買與生產之貨物減少時，本公司運輸之貨運量亦減少，且當公司將製造業移近消費市場並擴大分銷中心數量時，本公司運輸之貨運距離較短，這會重大且不利地影響本公司每貨運之營收與營運結果。部分製造商與零售商亦投資於在供應鏈與消費者較近之處生產與儲存貨物。此外，本公司業務規模與相對較高的固定成本結構（特別是與本公司航空網路相關），使本公司難以迅速調整以配合變動之貨運量。

自2022年底開始，美國進口消費性商品之減少，以及全球工業生產減緩，已導致運輸業持續處於較弱之營運條件，進而導致貨運量減少。此外，近期美國與國際貿易政策之變動亦進一步削弱運輸業之營運條件。通貨膨脹與高利率已對消費者與企業支出產生負面影響，本公司預期通貨膨脹與高利率將持續對本公司2026年財曆年度剩餘期間之營運結果產生負面影響。請參閱本年度報告之「項目7. 管理層對營運結果與財務狀況之討論與分析」以取得更多資訊。
此外，考量本公司業務性質及全球營運特性，外國國家及地區的政治、經濟及其他狀況，包括國際稅務、政府間關係、通常較為波動的新興市場經濟，以及地緣政治風險如俄羅斯與烏克蘭之間持續的衝突、美國與伊朗之間的衝突，以及其他

中東地區的衝突，可能對我們的業務及營運結果造成重大且不利的影響。例如，我們在烏克蘭的服務仍受限制，我們在白俄羅斯的服務仍處於中止狀態，我們已退出在俄羅斯的業務，且我們在中東地區的服務受到影響。這些衝突的廣泛影響、持續時間及演變性質，包括可能進一步的制裁、禁運、區域不穩定及地緣政治變動；與特定航線相關的空域禁飛措施，或戰略性決定改變某些航線；外國政府及其他團體對我們的潛在報復行動；以及美國與我們營運國家之間的緊張關係增加，均無法預測。

若俄羅斯與烏克蘭之間的持續衝突，以及美國與伊朗之間的衝突，以及中東地區的戰事，或隨後的類似衝突或戰事，對我們的業務造成重大且不利的影響，也可能導致許多其他在本年度報告中披露的風險加劇，任何這些風險均可能對我們的業務及營運結果造成重大且不利的影響。這些風險包括但不限於：對我們全球科技基礎設施的幹擾，包括透過網路攻擊或網路入侵、勒索軟體攻擊或惡意軟體攻擊；國際貿易政策的不利變動；燃料成本增加及供應不足；我們執行及落實業務策略的能力，特別是在國際業務方面；全球供應鏈的中斷，這可能限制聯邦快遞及我們的服務供應商對車輛及其他關鍵資本資源的取得，並增加我們的成本，也可能影響我們實現到2040年歷年財曆達成全球營運碳中和目標的能力；我們維持強大聲譽及聯邦快遞品牌價值的能力；針對運輸基礎設施的恐怖活動；我們對外幣波動的敞口；以及資本市場的限制、波動性或中斷。
